title: Exact Integrality Gap of the Held-Karp LP for Asymmetric TSP
short_statement: The asymmetric metric TSP Held-Karp integrality gap lies between $2$ and $17$; its exact value remains open.
open_problem: Determine the exact integrality gap of the Held-Karp LP for asymmetric metric TSP, closing the gap between the lower bound $2$ and the best known upper bound $17$.
background: Asymmetric TSP replaces undirected metrics by directed metrics, and this destroys the parity structure that makes Christofides' algorithm work. The standard Held-Karp LP is still the central relaxation: it enforces one unit of in-flow and out-flow at each vertex plus subtour-elimination constraints. For many years it was not even known whether this relaxation had a constant integrality gap. Svensson, Tarnawski, and Vegh proved the breakthrough constant-factor approximation, analyzed against the LP, thereby establishing a bounded gap. Traub and Vygen improved the bound first to $22$ and then to $17$ in their 2024 book. The lower bound remains only $2$. The exact integrality gap is therefore a major open quantitative question in directed network design.
full_statement: Let $(V,d)$ be a finite directed metric: $d(u,u)=0$ and $d(u,w)\le d(u,v)+d(v,w)$, but $d(u,v)$ need not equal $d(v,u)$. The asymmetric traveling salesperson problem asks for a minimum-cost directed Hamiltonian cycle. The Held-Karp relaxation has variables $x_{uv}\ge0$ for ordered pairs $u\ne v$, imposes one unit of outgoing and incoming flow at each vertex, and enforces subtour-elimination constraints $x(\delta^+(S))\ge1$ and $x(\delta^-(S))\ge1$ for every nonempty proper $S\subset V$. Its value is at most the optimum tour cost. The integrality gap is $$\sup_{(V,d)} \frac{\mathrm{OPT}_{\mathrm{ATSP}}(V,d)}{\mathrm{HK}(V,d)}.$$ Determine this supremum exactly. Current evidence leaves a broad interval: explicit directed metrics give gap at least $2$, while the best general rounding/approximation analysis gives gap at most $17$.
known_results: Charikar, Goemans, and Karloff constructed ATSP instances with Held-Karp integrality gap at least $2$, establishing the main lower-bound benchmark. Before 2018, general ATSP had only logarithmic approximation guarantees, and it was unknown whether the Held-Karp relaxation had any constant gap. Svensson, Tarnawski, and Vegh gave the first constant-factor approximation for general ATSP, implying a constant Held-Karp gap; their analysis yields an integrality-ratio upper bound of $319$ and an approximation factor $506$. Traub and Vygen simplified and strengthened the framework, improving the approximation ratio to $22+\epsilon$ and the Held-Karp integrality-gap upper bound to $22$. Traub and Vygen's 2024 book strengthens this to gap at most $17$ (Corollary 8.26), via a $(17+\epsilon)$-approximation relative to the LP (Theorem 8.25). The remaining interval is $[2,17]$.

progress.summary: The published Held-Karp gap interval is $[2,17]$; boundedness is resolved but the exact constant is not.

counterexample_rationale: Improved lower bounds are explicit directed metrics with large tour-to-LP ratio, and can be certified by LP and exact ATSP computations for finite instances.
alphaevolve_rationale: Search over small directed metrics or gadget compositions may find larger lower-bound instances. Algorithmic improvement requires proof-oriented rounding or connectivity-augmentation ideas.

literature.synthesis: The modern ATSP algorithms reduce global directed connectivity requirements to more local covering and augmentation problems, such as Subtour Partition Cover and structured vertebrate-pair instances. These reductions finally proved that the Held-Karp relaxation is constant-factor roundable, but the constants are far from the lower bound. The gap may reflect inefficiency in the decomposition/augmentation framework, or it may indicate missing lower-bound gadgets with much larger ratio than $2$. Progress likely requires either a sharper rounding of thin directed structures or a new family of directed metrics that exposes limitations of Held-Karp.

agent_guidance.suitable_approaches: For lower bounds, search directed metrics generated by layered gadgets, circulations, and asymmetric cuts. For upper bounds, focus on improving vertebrate-pair reductions or finding stronger augmentations of thin Eulerian subgraphs.
agent_guidance.verification_notes: A lower-bound instance must be a directed metric, not an arbitrary arc-cost digraph, and must certify both the Held-Karp LP value and the optimum tour cost. For finite computational lower bounds, the verifier should check the metric closure, solve or certify the LP, and certify optimal tour cost exactly or with rigorous bounds. An upper bound must round arbitrary feasible Held-Karp solutions for general ATSP; analyses for special cases such as graphic, node-weighted, or bounded-genus ATSP do not settle the standard gap.
